_readme: TWO PASSES, IN ORDER. Pass 1 is `inventory` — what is this source even about.
Pass 2 is `dimensions` — is it good enough to build from. Do not start pass 2 until
every inventory row is filled: a grade over a corpus you have not identified is a
grade of your own assumptions.
INVENTORY (pass 1), one row per file — EVERY file under sourceRoot, no format skipped —
filled by OPENING it:
kind:        docs | code | data | ui | contract | unknown
answers:     which dimension keys this source can speak to, e.g. ["domain","rules"].
Empty list is a real answer — say so rather than leaving it null.
statedScope: if the source declares its own boundary, quote it VERBATIM. Sources
that say what they do not cover are the cheapest scope signal there is.
components:  named modules/components/aggregates this source defines, one string each.
format/route/media/pages are stamped by init from bin/lib/source-formats.tsv — what the
file is by extension, the extraction route that consumes it whole, and how
many embedded images/diagrams a text-only read would leave behind. A row
with media > 0 is not consumed until its disposition accounts for them.
DISPOSITIONS (Stage 1) — one entry per inventory row (or a glob covering several), read
by bin/source-ledger.sh, which blocks the Stage 1 and 2 gates while any row has none:
{"path": "<rel>" | "pattern": "<glob over rel>", "state": "extracted",
"artifact": "<project-relative file or dir that carries what was extracted>",
"evidence": "<one specific finding that came OUT of the file, and where it landed>",
"media": <images described, must equal the row's media count, or "mediaWaived": "why">,
"by": "who", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
The artifact must exist, be non-empty, and NAME the source file — a disposition that
says 'the triage already used it' is checked by grepping the triage for the file, and
fails if it never mentions it. Write them with: bin/source-ledger.sh mark ...
A file deliberately not extracted is a register line, not a disposition:
bin/gate-check.sh <project> --waive source/<rel> --reason "..."
DIMENSIONS (pass 2). Fill in every dimension by READING the sources. Do not infer a
rating from file size.
rating: absent | named | specified | verified
evidence: where you saw it (page, section, screen) — or why you concluded absent.
consequence: what the BUILD has to invent if this stays as-is. Be concrete.
Leave rating null for any dimension you did not actually check; the report will
refuse to score rather than treat unchecked as absent.

actors.evidence: roles.md + 05-stakeholders-and-roles.html §2.1: four roles (Shipping Agent, Berth Officer, Harbour Master, Inspector), one role per user, Harbour Master's extra authority named explicitly (overrides, agent reactivation, tariff maintenance).
actors.consequence: none — actors and their authority boundaries are fully named, nothing to invent.

domain.demands: Entities, their attributes, and the relationships between them
domain.evidence: 07-domain-overview.html + 12/14/36 + glossary.md: 11 entities (Vessel, ShippingAgent, Terminal, Berth, BookingRequest, ApprovalDecision, Tariff, Invoice, Inspection, InspectionItem, AuditEntry) with typed/sized attributes and an explicit relationships list.
domain.consequence: none for the named entities. One field-level conflict to resolve at Stage 2: BookingRequest.Reference / Vessel.IMONumber size is 'up to 7 characters' in ch07/36 vs the validation screenshot's 'exactly 7 digits' — the build must pick one (screenshot is more specific, recommend that).

processes.demands: Flows and sequences: what happens after what, and what state it leaves behind
processes.evidence: 08-booking-lifecycle.html (status model, submission timing), 15-officer-review-process.html (queue/review), 22-24 (inspection flow), 25 (departure clearance) — a full state machine is describable end to end from Draft through Completed/departure.
processes.consequence: none — the process is fully walkable from the chapters; two internal contradictions exist within it (see 'processes' openQuestions raised at Stage 0/2), not gaps.

rules.demands: Business rules, validations, thresholds, calculations, eligibility criteria
rules.evidence: ~30 numbered business rules extracted verbatim across chapters 8-25 (fee calc, VAT, surcharges, fit check, suspension threshold, inspection outcome, etc.) — see analysis/rules-extract.md.
rules.consequence: two rules directly contradict each other (ch08 §4.4 fast-track auto-approval vs ch15 §11.4 'no automatic approval') and must be resolved by a human before build; recorded as an open question, resolved ASSUMED in this unattended run in favour of the more explicit ch15 statement.

ui.demands: Screens, navigation, layout, and which data appears on which
ui.evidence: 28-navigation-and-screens.html names the 3 nav screens; 29-31 describe Booking Board/My Bookings/Inspection Calendar; 09 and 21 carry actual prototype screenshots (mandatory fields, validation messages, exceedance highlight in red).
ui.consequence: none for the screens shown. Screens reached from elsewhere (Officer Review detail, Booking Request Form, Tariffs admin, Reporting) exist in the corpus but are not all in the 3-item nav list — Stage 3 wireframing should treat the nav row as the top level only, not the full screen inventory.

conflicts.title: Fast-track auto-approval vs. manual-review-only
conflicts.detail: 08-booking-lifecycle.md §4.4 states a booking is auto-approved when the berth is free for the whole stay and the vessel is under 120m LOA. 15-officer-review-process.md §11.4 states 'There is no automatic approval; every booking request is reviewed by a berth officer before it can become Approved.' Both are Revision 7 (current). Resolved ASSUMED in this unattended run in favour of §11.4 (the more explicit, unambiguous statement) — the fast-track rule is treated as superseded/stale content, not built. Cost if wrong: officers manually approve cases that could have auto-approved — a conservative, low-risk direction to be wrong in.

conflicts.title: Dangerous-goods approval gate vs. inspection-scheduling precondition
conflicts.detail: 22-inspection-scheduling.md §18.1 says an inspector schedules an inspection against an Approved booking (approval precedes scheduling, general case). §18.2 says a Dangerous Goods booking cannot be Approved until an inspection has been scheduled (scheduling precedes approval, for DG). Resolved ASSUMED in this unattended run as a DG-specific carve-out on the approval gate, not a true contradiction: for DG cargo the officer schedules the inspection while the booking is Under Review, then approves once it is scheduled. Cost if wrong: DG booking microflow's schedule/approve ordering would need to be reversed at Stage 5 — a single microflow, low cost.

choices.title: Cargo manifest PDF attachment on a booking request — never promoted to a chapter
choices.detail: workshop-notes.md session 2: 'Agents must be able to attach the cargo manifest as a PDF to a booking request' — attachment size limit explicitly 'not decided'. Absent from all 8 revisions of the numbered chapters. This changes the BookingRequest shape (a file association) if adopted. Resolved ASSUMED deferred/out-of-scope for the Stage 2 BRD in this unattended run — ADR-007 treats the chapters, not the raw workshop notes, as where requirements are settled, and 7 revisions have not adopted it. Cost if wrong: a real feature is missing from Stage 3 architecture and needs a retrofit (one file-association entity + one page control).

choices.title: 'Last five bookings of the same vessel' on the officer review screen — never promoted to a chapter
choices.detail: workshop-notes.md session 3: 'The review screen must show the last five bookings of the same vessel.' Absent from 21-officer-review-screen.md and every other chapter. Changes the review screen's data requirements (a vessel-history sub-list) if adopted. Resolved ASSUMED deferred/out-of-scope in this unattended run, same reasoning as above. Cost if wrong: one extra list widget on one page at Stage 5, low cost.
